newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish ORBIS hotel chain net almost doubled in '95.
newsitem.headline: Polish ORBIS hotel chain net almost doubled in '95.

text.p: Poland's largest hotel chain, the state-owned ORBIS SA, reported a net profit of 19.9 million zlotys last year, up from 10.9 million zlotys in 1994, the company said in its annual report.
Orbis, a tourist service giant in the communist era, is scheduled for privatisation next year.
"We are very happy with the results, especially that we are just before our privatisation," Orbis deputy president Ireneusz Weglowski told Reuters.
He said the privatisation ministry was expected to choose a firm which would advise it on ORBIS' sale by mid-September and that five companies had applied for the job.
Weglowski said that ORBIS' management would like the company to enter the Warsaw bourse in the first phase of the privatisation and later offer a stake to a foreign investor.
In 1995, ORBIS SA sales amounted to 440.1 million zlotys up from 346.5 million zlotys in 1994.
It has 54 hotels in Poland ranging from five-star to three star hotels with a total of 10,344 rooms and 18,279 beds.
It also has hotels in Kologne, London, Paris, New York, Brussels, Stockholm and Budapest. It holds a 49 percent stake in hotels in Vienna and Rome.
